title: Injective hypercover augmentation for sheaves of arbitrary rings
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], equipped with a precoverage $J$ containing isomorphisms, stable under composition and base change, and admitting pullbacks of its covering morphisms. Assume the Grothendieck topology generated by $J$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] is subcanonical: each representable presheaf $h_V(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,V)$ is a sheaf. Let $R$ be a sheaf of rings, not assumed commutative, on $\mathcal C$, and let $I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $W$ be an object of $\mathcal C$ and let $U_\bullet\to W$ be an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], with augmentation commuting with all simplicial operators. Assume the following local matching condition: for every $n$, every $T\to W$ and every family of maps from $T$ to the proper lower simplices of $U_n$ compatible with all simplicial operators and the augmentation, there is a covering sieve of $T$ on which that family is the restriction of a map to $U_n$. Equivalently, $h_{U_0}\to h_W$ is an epimorphism of sheaves of sets, and for each $p>0$ the map $h_{U_p}\to M_p$ is an epimorphism, where $M_p$ is the finite limit of the lower-degree representable sheaves giving compatible proper faces of a $p$-simplex over $W$. Define $C^p(U,I)=I(U_p)$ for $p\geq0$, zero for $p<0$, with differential $\delta^p=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j d_j^*$ and $R(W)$-module structure through $U_p\to W$. Then the canonical restriction augmentation $I(W)[0]\to C^\bullet(U,I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $R(W)$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Explicitly the augmented sequence $0\to I(W)\to I(U_0)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}I(U_1)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}I(U_2)\to\cdots$ is exact. No weak contractibility or affineness of the $U_p$ is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the represented free module presheaf explicitly as P_A(V)=R(V)[ULift Hom(V,A)] with restriction of both labels and coefficients. Sheafify to F_A. The explicit additive Yoneda equivalence sends a map P_A→M to its value on the identity generator; its inverse sends a generator [a] to restriction along a. Compose with the module-sheafification adjunction to obtain Hom(F_A,I) ≃+ I(A). Verify that precomposition with F(f) is section restriction and with an alternating boundary is the stated alternating sum. Use Mathlib’s alternating-face complex for the square-zero identities, and augmentation naturality for the augmented square-zero identity. The explicit construction handles module and coefficient universes which differ.

For a positive-degree finite-support cycle, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-hypercover-finite-local-cones] to its nonempty original support; the zero cycle is immediate. Extend its two cone functions additively, changing coefficients by restriction. On each generator the alternating sum gives ∂c+b∂=restriction: split the finite sum at index zero, then pair successor signs with the preceding boundary sum. Add over the original support. Since the original boundary is zero, the restricted cycle is a boundary. Cone functions remain indexed by original labels even when restriction coalesces them.

For degree zero, choose a representative vertex in each augmentation fibre. The kernel of the map on free presheaves is generated by differences between a vertex and its fibre representative: mapping the coefficient vector to representatives factors through its zero augmentation. The proved degree-one local_edge specialization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-hypercover-finite-local-cones] fills each difference. Induction on the finitely supported vector and finite intersections of covers make the original degree-zero cycle locally a boundary.

Prove directly that sheafification of a locally surjective module-presheaf map is epi. Under the adjunction, two maps out of its sheafification agree on every local lift, and sheaf separatedness makes them equal. For a short complex with local boundaries, apply this to its kernel lift. Module-presheaf kernels are sectionwise; sheafification preserves finite limits, so its kernel comparison is an isomorphism. Its sheafified kernel lift is therefore epi, which is Mathlib’s exact_iff_epi_kernel_lift criterion. This proves all free-sheaf short complexes exact without a separate lemma about locally represented sheafification sections.

Degree-zero matching lifts over W show that F(U_0)→F(W) is epi: use the Yoneda equivalence and separatedness to cancel it. For any exact short complex and injective I, a dual cocycle kills the first map. Apply ShortComplex.Exact.descToInjective to extend it across the last object; comp_descToInjective proves it is a dual boundary. The short-complex zero relation proves every dual boundary is a cocycle. Transport this exactness through the additive Yoneda equivalences and the verified alternating-boundary comparison. Epi cancellation gives injectivity of the augmentation. The target’s original function-level statement follows with every binder and universe unchanged.

theorem ringedHypercover_injective_augmentation_exact_ring
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition]
    [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks] [J.toGrothendieck.Subcanonical]
    (R : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck RingCat.{r})
    (I : ringedSiteModules.{max u v r} R) [Injective I]
    (W : C) (U : SimplicialObject C)
    (e : U ⟶ (Functor.const SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ).obj W)
    (hcover : ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : C) (w : T ⟶ W)
      (p : ∀ (Δ : SimplexCategory), Δ.len < n →
        (Δ ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n) → (T ⟶ U.obj (op Δ))),
      (∀ (Δ : SimplexCategory) (h : Δ.len < n) (θ : Δ ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n),
        p Δ h θ ≫ e.app (op Δ) = w) →
      (∀ (Δ Δ' : SimplexCategory) (h : Δ.len < n) (h' : Δ'.len < n)
        (α : Δ' ⟶ Δ) (θ : Δ ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n),
        p Δ h θ ≫ U.map α.op = p Δ' h' (α ≫ θ)) →
      ∃ S : Sieve T, S ∈ J.toGrothendieck T ∧
        ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ T), S f →
          ∃ t : V ⟶ U _⦋n⦌,
            t ≫ e.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk n)) = f ≫ w ∧
            ∀ (Δ : SimplexCategory) (h : Δ.len < n) (θ : Δ ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n),
              t ≫ U.map θ.op = f ≫ p Δ h θ) :
    Function.Injective (I.val.map (e.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))).op) ∧
    Function.Exact
      (I.val.map (e.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))).op)
      (fun s : I.val.obj (op (U _⦋0⦌)) ↦
        ∑ j : Fin 2, (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val • I.val.map (U.δ j).op s) ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Exact
      (fun s : I.val.obj (op (U _⦋n⦌)) ↦
        ∑ j : Fin (n + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val • I.val.map (U.δ j).op s)
      (fun s : I.val.obj (op (U _⦋n + 1⦌)) ↦
        ∑ j : Fin (n + 3), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val • I.val.map (U.δ j).op s)
